elements.name: question72
elements.html:
Protocol: V175-001

Phase: 1

 

Opening

Thank you for your interest in our vaccine clinical trials! As you may know, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and parainfluenza virus (PIV3) are major contributors to infections and diseases such as pneumonia or influenza-like illnesses. These three infections can often go hand in hand and significantly raise the mortality associated with lower respiratory tract diseases, and there currently is no approved vaccine to help protect against all three. As such, this trial is being conducted to assess the safety and efficiency of a potential vaccine that synthesises all three infections.

elements.name: question78
elements.html:
Study Drug and Design

As mentioned, the study drug is a combination vaccine against RSV, hMPV and PIV3 and will be compared against both a placebo and existing RSV vaccine, Arexvy. Depending on which group you’re placed in, you can receive either one of these. As the study is double blinded, neither you or the study team will know which you’ve received until the end of the trial.

elements.name: question80
elements.html:
Study Schedule

 

Participants can expect this study to last for up to 12 months, with up to 9 visits to the clinic in Botany, and up to 2 telehealth calls.

 

These 9 in-clinic visits consist of the following schedule:

 

  • Screening visit (screening period can take up to 28 days)
  • 3 visits and 2 phone calls on the following days in the first month:
    • Day 1
    • Day 2
    • Day 3 - telehealth call
    • Day 8 (+/- 1 day)
    • Day 15 - telehealth call
  • 1 visit in each quarterly month thereafter:
    • Day 29 (+/- 2 days)
    • Day 90 (+/- 1 week)
    • Day 180 (+/- 2 weeks)
    • Day 270 (+/- 2 weeks)
    • Day 365 (+/- 2 weeks)

 

Your initial screening visit is expected to last for up to 3 hours. Once found eligible, you will attend your dosing visit, which consists of pre and post-dose monitoring and assessments, totalling the visit to about 5 hours.

elements.name: question82
elements.html:
Reimbursement

You will be reimbursed the following for any reasonable travel, parking, meals, and other expenses associated with your study visits, broken down as follows:

 

• $250 for the Screening Visit

• $540 for Day 1 (Vaccination Visit)

• $300 for In-Clinic Follow Up Visits on Day 2, Day 8, Day 29, Day 90, Day 180, Day 270 and Day 365

• $50 for a Telephone Call on Day 15

 

At the end of the study, you will be reimbursed $500.

 

If you attend all scheduled visits, you can be reimbursed up to $3,440 upon completion of the study.

 

If required by the trial protocol, you may have a Telephone Call on Day 3. If this is required, your

trial doctor will let you know. You will be reimbursed $50 for the Day 3 Telephone Call.

 

During the study, you may have an unscheduled visit if the study team deems it necessary. You will

be reimbursed $300 for unscheduled visits.

elements.name: question88
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before we even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.name: question109
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question108
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
